video_title: Anthropic IPOs As Markets Wait On A Slowdown | Weekly Roundup
gist: Forward Guidance hosts argue the roughly $2T Anthropic IPO is a 'now or never' listing with heavy unlock supply and capped upside as token prices fall, amid an AI build-out unwind (Nvidia down ~40%, AI credit seizing up). They see a late-hawkish Fed (Waller's 50bp talk) and a post-midterm administration with no incentive to prop markets, implying a slow-bleed growth slowdown with counter-trend rallies, while staying patient on bonds, gold and Bitcoin.

themes.theme: Anthropic IPO: supply overhang and capped upside

insights.claim: The SpaceX IPO, at a roughly trillion-dollar valuation, marked the top of a 30%+ Nasdaq rally off the March Iran-war lows, and the Anthropic IPO is arriving into a similarly heavy, weakening market.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Mega-IPOs absorb liquidity and have coincided with local tops; treat mega-cap private listings as potential sentiment/supply top signals.
insights.quote: the SpaceX IPO, which was I guess slightly bigger valuation, but smaller capital raise topped the Nasdaq at at its arrival

insights.claim: Headline oversubscription of the Anthropic IPO says little about demand quality because allocators routinely overbid to secure partial fills they intend to flip, and widespread retail ('normie') interest suggests the deal needed to dig deep for buyers.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Discount oversubscription headlines; broad retail participation in a mega-IPO is a warning sign for post-listing performance.
insights.quote: Yeah, the over subscribing thing is such a a BS thing.

insights.claim: Anthropic listed at about a $2 trillion valuation with a lock-up/unlock schedule described as more aggressive than SpaceX's, including some day-one unlocks and bigger chunks unlocking roughly twice as fast, creating ongoing selling supply.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host / Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Track the Anthropic unlock calendar as a source of recurring supply pressure on the stock and on AI-adjacent equities.
insights.quote: the unlock schedule for for Anthropic is a lot more aggressive than SpaceX, which was already very aggressive

insights.claim: Ramp data shows total AI token usage still skyrocketing while business spend on tokens is flat, implying falling per-token prices and a shift away from high-margin frontier-model usage.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Volume growth is not translating into revenue growth for frontier labs; watch spend vs. usage data as the key fundamental for AI-lab valuations.
insights.quote: total token usage is still skyrocketing. But if you go to the spend, it's flat.

insights.claim: Because token prices only move down, a frontier lab IPOing at $2 trillion is a 'now or never' event with limited upside; getting to $3 trillion would require something like regulatory-captured AGI or proprietary breakthroughs such as curing cancer.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Asymmetric downside for frontier-lab equity at current valuations; avoid paying up for AI-lab IPOs.
insights.quote: for me, it's like these frontier models, if they want to IPO 2 trillion bucks, it's now or never. And the upside just feels really limited.

insights.claim: Compute and tokens are becoming a commodity, and commodity producers are price takers whose margins get competed down to marginal cost, so usage must grow explosively just to offset repeated halvings in per-token cost.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Frame AI model providers and compute sellers as commodity businesses when valuing them.
insights.quote: Commodities are by definition you're a price taker as a producer. You're not a maker.

insights.claim: The hosts argue the retail-access regime is failing investors: retail can gamble on any event in Robinhood and Coinbase yet only gets access to companies at trillion-dollar valuations after late private rounds, which they link to the political appeal of regulators like Elizabeth Warren.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Regulatory backlash risk for retail brokerages and prediction-market/IPO-access business models under a Democratic Congress.

themes.theme: AI build-out unwind: Nvidia, credit and shifting incentives

insights.claim: Semiconductors have been in a bear market since July and Nvidia, described as the 'AI central bank' and biggest circular-financing provider, fell about 40% in under 40 days from a 6+ trillion dollar market cap.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: The collapse of Nvidia's equity currency weakens its ability to finance the AI ecosystem, a reflexive negative for downstream players.
insights.quote: the AI Central Bank Nvidia, their share price would plummet at 40% in less than 40 days

insights.claim: Credit markets are seizing up for the AI build-out vertical; neoclouds and data-center operators with capex commitments the size of their market caps can no longer tap unsecured debt and will have to raise equity.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Expect dilutive equity raises and distress among capital-intensive AI infrastructure names; avoid weak capital structures.
insights.quote: They can't they can't tap into the unsecured debt markets at in this environment.

insights.claim: Nvidia's new CEO, on his first earnings call, signaled more pragmatism on financing deals, putting at risk downstream companies whose financing rested on informal handshake agreements with Jensen.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Downstream beneficiaries of Nvidia vendor financing face funding risk; scrutinize who depends on Nvidia-backed deals.
insights.quote: if I if I was one of those downstream companies and my only agreement is over a couple of glasses of wine with Jensen and a handshake, like I would be a bit worried right now

insights.claim: When a bubble cracks, previously aligned incentives flip: hyperscalers or Nvidia could pull contracts from a data-center provider to crush its stock and buy it cheaply, and Elon's bearish CoreWeave tweets are read as positioning to buy it out at a deep discount.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host / Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Expect predatory consolidation in AI infrastructure over the next few years; firms with unhealthy capital structures become targets.
insights.quote: I think that's what Elon is doing when he tweets about being bearish CoreWeave.

insights.claim: The hosts flag lingering denial in sentiment: midsummer consensus held that semis were no longer cyclical and memory had not topped, a classic bubble-top narrative they had called in July.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: 'This time it's not cyclical' narratives in semis remain a reliable top signal; persistent denial suggests capitulation is not complete.

insights.claim: Despite a growth slowdown, bonds have barely rallied (yields only 30-40bp lower at the recent low) while the Nasdaq is down about 15-16% and the Russell about 13-14%, showing rising correlations and that the weakness is no longer just an AI trade.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Slowdown hedges are not yet paying; broadening equity weakness signals a macro, not sector, drawdown.
insights.quote: the Nasdaq's down like 15 16, the Russell's down like 13 14

insights.claim: Fed minutes now flag AI-driven downstream inflation just as the build-out is slowing, and talk of 50bp hikes at the turn is the classic policy error that converts a slowdown into a recession.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Rising recession risk from a late-hawkish Fed; position for an eventual growth scare and later pivot.
insights.quote: that's the most classic Fed situation ever, and it's also how you get these policy error errors that go from a slowdown to recession

insights.claim: Waller's repeated threats of 50bp hikes, when rates markets price only about 5% odds of a December 50bp hike, are preventing bonds and precious metals from rallying; much of the hawkish rhetoric comes from presidents like Goolsbee who rotate off voting in January, while Williams is the most dovish.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Fed-speak headline risk is suppressing duration and gold; the January voter rotation could soften the hawkish tone.
insights.quote: the rates market is saying 5% odds of a 50 bips hike in December

insights.claim: Inflation topped in May, oil is down about 35%, crack spreads are crushed and the commodity complex is in the gutter, yet the Fed is only now voicing concerns markets flagged months ago, reflecting backward-looking policy despite 'long and variable lags'.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: The Fed is behind the curve on disinflation; falling commodity prices support an eventual dovish turn.
insights.quote: oil's down 35% crack spreads are crushed gasoline's down

insights.claim: Most of the move higher in the yield curve reflects Fed rate-path expectations rather than unanchored inflation or term premium, per charts cited from a prior guest (Aiden), with about three and a half more hikes priced in.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Long-end yields will fall quickly if the hike path is repriced; the rate path is the dominant driver to watch.
insights.quote: most of the move higher in the curve has been Fed rate policy expectations, not unanchoring of inflation or term premium

insights.claim: The Fed ran about $40 billion a month of reserve management purchases from December to mid-year, which flowed into semiconductors (110% moves in some mega-caps), then withdrew it, leaving real rates near GFC-era levels.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Liquidity withdrawal plus high real rates is a headwind for the most liquidity-sensitive assets that rallied on it.
insights.quote: they did 40 billion a month of RMPs December to mid year this year. What the heck? It all went into semiconductors.

themes.theme: Post-midterm politics: no put from Treasury or White House

insights.claim: Bessent's Treasury, which actively propped markets before the midterms via bond, FX and commodity interventions and buybacks, has gone radio silent, and the administration has incentive to let the decline run and blame Democrats while pressuring the Fed.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Do not count on a fiscal/Treasury put near term; relief is more likely to come from monetary policy.
insights.quote: this is the first decline of 2.0 second presidency that was not man-made effectively

insights.claim: The midterms acted as a starting gun rather than a clearing event, with a blowup two days after and a steady bleed since, and incentives to prop markets have swung sharply from pre- to post-midterm.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Be patient; the political incentive to support asset prices has weakened.

insights.claim: Letting equities and the AI build-out roll over may be the only way to get inflation below 2%, since crushing housing further will not do it, so a Warsh-led Fed may tolerate the slowdown while eventually backstopping key AI companies.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Fed tolerance for equity weakness is higher than markets assume; the Fed put strike is lower.
insights.quote: if you crush the AI build out and equities roll over that's how you get sub 2%

insights.claim: Cantor's 13F filing reportedly shows it sold Nvidia about a month ago and bought puts, which the hosts frame as politically connected insiders being the only winners.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host) / Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Watch 13F filings of politically connected firms for positioning signals.

insights.claim: The best inflation outcome is a slow, controlled, drawn-out decline rather than a COVID-style crash and V-bottom; this implies a possibly bigger peak-to-trough fall, a relief rally into January-February, another leg down, then a pause and maybe cuts late next year.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Expect a long chop with counter-trend rallies; sell rallies rather than chase a V-bottom.
insights.quote: you don't want a minus 30% market boom out. Like that doesn't really fix inflation

insights.claim: The host sees a decent chance of recession within about a year, but expects a possibly vicious year-end equity rally first, with bad economic data surfacing in February-March, so it is too early to put on recession bond positions.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Time recession trades (long duration) for early next year; a seasonal rally may offer better entry for shorts.
insights.quote: suddenly in February, March, you start to see the really bad economic data

insights.claim: Spending decisions for this quarter were made two quarters ago in 'AI trade land'; cancellations and slowdowns will hit real-economy building, spending and hiring in Q1-Q2, while housing starts keep falling and the main street economy is weak outside AI.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Expect lagged deterioration in macro data in H1; housing and capex-linked sectors are vulnerable.

insights.claim: A new regime has emerged where risk assets and oil fall together on growth fears, reversing the past six months when lower oil fueled rallies; Druckenmiller is short copper because markets signal growth trouble next year.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Treat oil-down/risk-down days as confirmation of a growth scare; copper weakness is a growth signal.
insights.quote: Druckenmiller was in an a interview this week

insights.claim: Today's setup mixes 2022 (an inflation/stagflation problem) and Q4 2018 (new hawkish Fed chair hiking into a turn with a soft labor market), but lacks 2022's offsets: 2022 payrolls ran above 500k a month January-April versus a recent high of about 130k now.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host / Quinn (co-host)
insights.so_what: Without a strong labor market cushion, hikes will bite growth faster than in 2022; the recipe could be worse than both precedents.
insights.quote: January to to April we printed over 500k jobs per month of of 2022

themes.theme: Gold, Bitcoin and crypto: wait for slowdown confirmation

insights.claim: The host is staying out of gold and Bitcoin despite a long-term bullish view, because both are bleeding weekly and stablecoin supply has seen persistent outflows since the Binance hack, delaying crypto fundamental excitement.
insights.speaker: Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Wait for slowdown confirmation and stablecoin inflows before buying gold or Bitcoin; avoid knife-catching.
insights.quote: if you look at like a chart of stable coin supply, like that's just been outflows and outflows

insights.claim: Heavy-handed administration intervention produced boom-bust cycles in metals, semis and energy this year, so any trade held a few days too long is exposed to policy reversals; both hosts side with Druckenmiller in pulling back and waiting.
insights.speaker: Quinn (co-host) / Forward Guidance host
insights.so_what: Reduce position sizes and holding periods; favor patience and cash in a policy-driven chop.
insights.quote: I'm in Druckenmiller's camp. It's just too much noise, too many uncertainties.
